data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following a checklist is more reliable than a single expert because the checklist converts tacit, error-prone intuition into an explicit, auditable process that eliminates single-point cognitive failure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires synthesis of contradictory evidence that cannot be decomposed into a linear checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is insufficiently granular to capture the 'edge cases' that the expert's intuition naturally flags.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Cognitive Load Distribution' mechanism: checklists decompose complex judgments into atomic, verifiable steps, reducing the working memory load on any single individual and replacing the expert's 'pattern matching' (which is susceptible to availability bias) with a 'systematic scan' (which ensures coverage).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
